status_summary: Executive Order 14154 (signed 2025-01-20) disbanded the Interagency Working Group on the Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases, withdrew its estimates and guidance, and revoked twelve earlier orders including Executive Order 14008, which had established the Office of Domestic Climate Policy; the order states that offices established in the revoked orders are abolished. It gave EPA 60 days to issue guidance addressing the social cost of carbon calculation, which may include considering its elimination from permitting and regulatory decisions; a separate EPA guidance document was not found. OMB's regulatory office, in consultation with EPA, issued memorandum M-25-27 (dated 2025-05-05), which says monetized analysis of greenhouse gas emissions will be needed in few if any cases and that agencies quantifying emissions should not monetize them, says a uniform federal estimate is no longer policy, points to the 2003 Circular A-4 where a value is required, and tells agencies to modify or rescind non-statutory greenhouse gas requirements as quickly as feasible. A final NHTSA fuel-economy rule published 2026-09-30 (effective 2026-11-30) set the social cost of carbon to zero in its analysis. Rather than a Senior Advisor, Executive Order 14213 (signed 2025-02-14) created a National Energy Dominance Council chaired by the Interior Secretary, whose functions report to the Office of the Chief of Staff and center on energy production, permitting and regulatory burdens.

timeline.event: Baseline: Executive Order 14008 establishes the White House Office of Domestic Climate Policy (Sec. 202), headed by the National Climate Advisor, and the National Climate Task Force (Sec. 203).

Executive Order 14154 (published 2025-01-29) disbands the social cost of greenhouse gases working group and withdraws its estimates (Sec. 6(b)), revokes twelve orders including 14008 and 13990, and abolishes offices established under them (Sec. 4(a)). It directs EPA to issue guidance considering elimination of the social cost of carbon from permitting and regulatory decisions (Sec. 6(c)); until then agencies use the 2003 Circular A-4 approach (Sec. 6(d)).

Executive Order 14213 (published 2025-02-20) creates the National Energy Dominance Council in the EOP, chaired by the Interior Secretary with the Energy Secretary as vice chair, with members including the EPA Administrator, the CEQ Chairman and the OSTP Director. Its functions report to the Office of the Chief of Staff, and the order does not mention the Office of Domestic Climate Policy.

DOE publishes a request for information on revising its energy conservation Process Rule that summarizes Executive Order 14154's direction on greenhouse gas valuation, notes the current rule uses Circular A-4, and says DOE expects to seek separate comment on emission estimates and monetization. Comments were due 2025-06-02.

OMB's Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs issues memorandum M-25-27 implementing Sec. 6 of Executive Order 14154, in consultation with EPA: monetized analysis of greenhouse gas emissions will be needed in few if any cases, agencies quantifying emissions should not monetize them, it is no longer federal policy to keep a uniform estimate, the 2003 Circular A-4 applies where Sec. 6(d) requires a value, and agencies should modify or rescind non-statutory greenhouse gas requirements as quickly as feasible. The date is the one stated in the memorandum text.

NHTSA publishes the final SAFE Vehicles Rule III (effective 2026-11-30); its model inputs set the social cost of carbon to zero, and it describes the action as consistent with Executive Orders 14154 and 14148.
